disposition: Consume the initial batch: the refined two-step solve is a solver-grid solution only. Its unsoftened holding speed sits at 98.7% of the 0.02 m/s limit while its independent BDF replay shows 0.043122 m/s holding speed and 2.449 mm node tip disagreement, so replay gates fail and no trustworthy feasible schedule exists. Among the permitted levers, substeps is already at its maximum (2), the position/speed weights are inert because the gap term is identically zero at the returned slack-zero point, and a design change targets a different question (d=0 already reaches NLP-grid feasibility and historically beat d=0.767). The only lever that can select a better-margined member of this degenerate slack-zero feasible set is the secondary effort/variation regularizer, so I request ONE revision solve with objective_mode task_gap_with_effort, secondary_coefficient at its allowed maximum 0.001, everything else unchanged (d=0 frozen, weights 1.0/1.0, substeps 2, warm start from the just-returned candidate), plus its one independent BDF replay. Then STOP.
fixed_conditions: Unchanged frozen study: target [0.29,0.035,0.19] m, mount [0,0,0.15] identity quaternion, gravity -9.81 m/s^2, 0.35 s over 35 control intervals of 0.01 s (physical timestep 0.0005 s, 24 cells), named zero initial positions and velocities (hard), existing two-segment topology with six ideal tension channels, guides, rigid parts and payload, existing material/sections and structural_linear basis, tension bounds [0,8] N hard, constant design along the trajectory within the given rule and domain, two shared nonnegative task slacks as the only relaxation, slack never subtracted at acceptance, exact automatic AD outer derivatives with retained local reverse, no physical launches, no integrator substitution, no controller search, no change to task, material, topology or horizon.
hypothesis: The returned refined-grid point is one arbitrary member of a degenerate optimal set, which is why its speed margin is razor-thin. Evidence: at substeps=2 the solve reports hard_max_normalized_violation 9.99e-9 with slack_values position/speed both about -1e-8 (pinned at their zero bound, so effectively unused), original_task_gaps position 0.0 and speed 0.0, and selected_search_objective -1.998e-08, i.e. the gap objective is identically zero at that point, so it cannot prefer any slack-zero feasible point over another and the iterate lands at 98.7% of the holding-speed limit (0.019742 vs 0.02 m/s). Secondary effort/variation regularization is the only permitted mechanism that gives the search a preference inside that feasible set; with coefficient 0.001 it stays far below the unit slack penalty (so slacks should remain zero) while rewarding lower-amplitude, smoother tension histories, which plausibly restores holding-speed margin and thereby reduces the continuum-versus-grid bias that dominates the replay error (speed 0.0466 m/s versus tip 2.46 mm).
limitations: This will be the second and final full NLP attempt; if it returns no usable schedule, no further solve is available.

substeps=2 is the maximum permitted refinement, so the activity cannot test whether the replay mismatch vanishes under further grid refinement; the observed reduction (8.106 mm to 2.449 mm node tip, 0.0997 to 0.0307 m/s speed) is consistent with slow convergence but does not establish the 0.005 s grid as converged.
Design stays frozen at d=0, so nothing here speaks to joint design/control behavior and corrected_B's worse d=0.767 point is not re-tested.
The secondary effort/variation term is a weighted tradeoff, not lexicographic; a smoother iterate is not guaranteed to realize a larger true (continuum) speed margin.

Agreement with SciPy BDF on one schedule at default tolerances is a numerical consistency check, not physical validation; zero physical launches are authorized, so task success on hardware is not established.
Slacks are search-only; a returned relaxed iterate, even with slack at zero, is not by itself task success without the replay gates and unsoftened metrics.
Single seed (17) and a single warm-start lineage: solution multiplicity at the refined grid is only partly probed.
Feasibility of the residual activity, any speedup, and second-batch behavior are not required or implied.
revision_or_stop_rule: This is the single revision batch. After consuming its solve and independent replay: (a) if the returned schedule keeps slack at zero and the replay meets both gates (node/dense tip disagreement under 1 mm, speed disagreement under 0.002 m/s) with unsoftened holding/terminal position under 0.01 m and holding speed under 0.02 m/s, report that bounded numerical result as the outcome and STOP; (b) if the replay still exceeds a gate or the unsoftened limits, record the two-candidate comparison (original grid versus refined grid, with and without effort regularization) as the result and STOP, with no further solve; (c) if the revision returns only failure or unusable output, interpret that honestly and STOP. No third NLP attempt, no design search, and at most one further diagnostic replay only if a genuinely new candidate question arises.
weakening_observation: The refinement did not buy acceptance. Solving the frozen-design slack problem on the refined two-step grid moved the iterate to a point that is unsoftened-feasible on the solver grid (holding position 0.005515 m, terminal 0.005515 m, holding speed 0.019742 m/s, all inside limits, slack effectively zero) but its independent BDF replay exceeds both replay gates: node_max_tip_disagreement 0.002449 m and node_max_speed_disagreement 0.030684 m/s (dense 0.002460 m and 0.046612 m/s), gates_passed false, and the replay's own holding speed is 0.043122 m/s (sampled evaluator 0.037135 m/s), roughly double the 0.02 m/s task limit. The same comparison on the original grid was 0.008106 m and 0.0997 m/s, so refinement helps but remains far outside gates, and the returned point has essentially no speed margin (0.019742 versus 0.02, about 1.3% headroom). This weakens any claim that solver-grid feasibility transfers to the continuous model at the maximum permitted refinement.
